claims.text: The initial as-cast Mg-containing lightweight HEA is a non-equilibrium, metastable, single-phase solid solution.
Thermal aging drives diffusion-mediated segregation of Mg and other solutes.
Solute segregation triggers the nucleation and growth of nanoscale intermetallic precipitates.
The precipitates are Al- or Cr-rich phases modified by Mg segregation.
Intermetallic precipitates nucleate preferentially at grain boundaries and dislocations.
Moderate aging at 300–450°C and intermediate temperatures produces discrete nanoscale intermetallic precipitates.
Isolated intermetallic precipitates act as preferential nucleation sites for passivating oxides.
Passivation associated with isolated precipitates maintains or slightly enhances corrosion resistance relative to the as-cast state.
Passivation associated with isolated precipitates maintains or slightly enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast state.
Aging at or above approximately 600°C produces a continuous, interconnected intermetallic network.
Prolonged aging can cause intermetallic precipitates to coalesce into percolating networks.
A percolating intermetallic network disrupts formation of a uniform protective oxide barrier.
Disruption of the oxide barrier by an interconnected intermetallic network degrades high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Disruption of the oxide barrier by an interconnected intermetallic network degrades corrosion resistance.
Below approximately 600°C, transformation kinetics are slow and passivation benefits prevail.
At or above approximately 600°C, or after prolonged aging, intermetallic connectivity becomes detrimental.
Aging in an inert to mildly oxidizing atmosphere isolates thermal-diffusional transformation kinetics.
The time and temperature of the beneficial-to-detrimental transition may depend on alloy composition and processing history.
The as-cast state is the control for comparing microstructure, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance after aging.
Failure to form the predicted precipitates, or failure of precipitate connectivity to correlate with the predicted performance changes, would falsify the hypothesis.
